Evaluation on a quadrotor altitude regulation task demonstrates that Flip-Team achieves lower cost than always-human and always-autonomous baselines, with selective authority switching that balances human adaptability and autonomous efficiency.

Baselines: We compare four strategies: 1) Always-autonomous: Autonomous agent controls throughout ( α k = A , ∀ k ). 2) Always-human: Human controls throughout ( α k = H , ∀ k ). 3) Performance-threshold: Switch to human when tracking error ∥ x k ∥ exceeds a threshold ε = 1 . 0; switch back when ∥ x k ∥ < ε . 4) Flip-Team : Optimal switching policy from Theorem 1 with known p k .
This paper presents Flip-Team , a cooperative framework for authority switching in shared autonomy.
